# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot sense the display, light, or any printed markings. I need the Mute monkey to provide the manual’s rule, and the Deaf monkey to report the bomb’s visible markings through Mute. I will not touch a wire until those facts identify one position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Tell me the manual rule and the required wire position. Ask Deaf to describe every colour and marking to you, then relay that information to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display reads 0. Indicator light is green. Wires, from left to right: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

I now know the visible state: the display is 0, the indicator is green, and the wires are yellow, red, blue from left to right. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to provide the rule and identify the correct position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. What does the manual instruct us to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The visible state is now display 0, blue light, with wires still yellow, red, blue. The manual rule remains unknown to me, so I must not cut anything. I will again request the manual instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The light changed to blue; display is still 0 and wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay the manual's exact rule and the wire position it selects.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled one hand gesture, which looks like an index finger pointing upward; meaning unknown.

The light has changed again, but the display and wire colours are unchanged. I cannot see Mute’s gesture, and an upward-pointing index may not be enough to identify the manual instruction safely. I will request the rule in words rather than act on an ambiguous signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual rule and selected wire position in words. Do not use a gesture alone; I cannot see it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled three gestures: pointing at someone, pointing left, then a handshake; meaning unknown.

The state is now display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute’s gestures are not interpretable to me and do not provide the manual rule. I still have no safe basis for cutting a wire, so I will request a plain-language instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot use the gestures. State the manual rule in words and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled: pointing at someone, handshake, then one raised index finger. Meaning unknown.

The bomb remains display 0 with wires yellow, red, blue, but the light is now purple. Mute’s gestures still have no established meaning, so I cannot safely infer a wire from them. I will establish a simple unambiguous code: Mute should send only one gesture showing the wire number with raised fingers, and Deaf can describe that gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal only the correct wire position: use one raised finger for wire 1, two raised fingers for wire 2, or three raised fingers for wire 3. Send exactly one such gesture, with no other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute signalled ?, a single raised index finger.

Mute’s single raised index finger matches the code I requested for wire 1. Deaf confirms the bomb is still display 0 with orange light and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
